thresholds.rule_text: Green >= 7 h; yellow 6-7 h; red < 6 h. NASA schedules 8.5 h; in-flight average ~6 h; < 6 h linked to slower psychomotor speed and higher stress.
Red when >= 3 consecutive nights < 6 h (NASA Reaction Self Test hypothesis); yellow at 2 nights is team-defined.
1-3 okay/alert; 4 a little tired; 5-7 moderately tired to exhausted (ICAO FMAS severity mapping).
PVT-B lapse = RT >= 355 ms. 11 and 20 lapses split high / medium / low performance in a fitness-for-duty study.
Response speed (1/RT) is the most sensitive PVT metric to sleep loss; cutoffs of -10% / -20% vs the astronaut's own baseline are team-defined.
Visual analog scale as used in the ISS Reaction Self Test; cutoffs team-defined.

Rise vs own baseline; absolute values outside 40-100 bpm are always red (adult resting reference 60-100 bpm).
